patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents requesting prenatal care, reporting 2 months of increasing breast tenderness, nausea, a 6.6 lb weight gain, increased urinary frequency, and uncertainty about the date of her last menstrual period. She stopped taking oral contraceptives 6 months ago and has been trying to conceive with her husband since then. She believes she is pregnant and was happy to share this news with her husband last week.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Stopped oral contraceptives 6 months prior in an attempt to conceive.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Reports being in a stable relationship and actively trying to conceive with her husband.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with symptoms suggestive of early pregnancy.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m coming in because I think I might be pregnant—I’ve had increasing breast tenderness for about two months, along with nausea and about a 6.6 lb weight gain. I’m also urinating more often, and I’m not sure exactly when my last period was since I stopped oral contraceptives six months ago and have been trying to conceive.
I’m glad you came in. To start, have you had any vaginal bleeding or spotting since stopping the oral contraceptives?
“No, I haven’t noticed any vaginal bleeding or spotting since stopping the oral contraceptives.”
Do you know the date of your last menstrual period (LMP) or have you had any menstrual-like bleeding since stopping the pill?
I don’t know the exact date of my last menstrual period, and I haven’t had any menstrual-like bleeding or spotting since stopping the pill.
Have you had any abdominal or pelvic pain (such as lower‑abdominal cramping, flank pain, or pelvic discomfort) that’s new or worsening?
“No, I haven’t had any abdominal or pelvic pain, and I don’t have flank pain or pelvic discomfort.”
When did you first start trying to conceive, and have you had regular unprotected intercourse (e.g., every 2–3 days) since stopping the pill?

I started trying to conceive right after I stopped the oral contraceptives about six months ago, and we’ve been having unprotected intercourse pretty regularly, roughly every couple of days. I haven’t noticed any unusual symptoms like bleeding or significant pain—mostly just the breast tenderness, nausea, weight gain, and needing to urinate more often.
Have you taken a home pregnancy test yet, and if so, what was the result?
“I haven’t taken a home pregnancy test yet—I wasn’t sure if it was early, and I wanted to come in to confirm.”
Do you have any urinary symptoms such as burning, urgency, pain, or fever that might suggest an infection?
“No, I haven’t had burning or pain when I pee, and I haven’t had any fever—just increased urinary frequency.”

Have you had any prior pregnancies, miscarriages, ectopic pregnancies, or surgeries/infections (such as pelvic inflammatory disease or tubal surgery) that might affect your risk for an ectopic pregnancy?
“I’ve never been pregnant before, and I haven’t had any miscarriages or ectopic pregnancies. I also haven’t had any pelvic surgeries or infections like pelvic inflammatory disease.”

Do you have any other symptoms such as palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, or unexplained weight loss that might suggest a thyroid issue, or any chronic medical conditions (e.g., diabetes, hypertension) or medications you’re currently taking?

“No, I don’t have palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, or unexplained weight loss. I don’t have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or hypertension, and I’m not taking any medications right now since stopping the oral contraceptives.”
[DDX] Early intrauterine pregnancy, Ectopic pregnancy (early, without pain), Ovarian cyst (functional), Hyperprolactinemia, Early thyroid dysfunction
